targets.authors: Hickok, G., Farahbod, H., & Saberi, K.
targets.title: The rhythm of perception: Entrainment to acoustic rhythms induces subsequent perceptual oscillation.
targets.evidence_quote: The primary goal of the current study was to replicate the entrainment effect observed in Hickok et al. (2015).
targets.outcome_quote: Neither experiment revealed significant entrainment effects at the group level.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Both the conceptual and exact replication failed to show the original central group-level entrainment effect; positive results in a subset do not overturn the authors’ conclusion.

reasoning: Title, DOI and all three authors match. Primary record type is replication because two independent new samples re-test Hickok et al. (2015). The paper also reanalyses the original data with modified quantitative methods as a calibration/reference step; that component confirms the original positive effect and is distinguished from the failed new-sample replications. Other entrainment studies and the Dryad data release are not additional originals.

secondary_reproduction_component.outcome_computational_quote: We first analysed the data from the original study of Hickok et al. (2015), using the modified analysis pipeline.
secondary_reproduction_component.outcome_robustness_quote: In summary, reanalysis of the data from the original study using our quantitative methods confirmed the observation of a positive entrainment effect (normalized 2.67-Hz power) in all participants’ hit rate curves.
secondary_reproduction_component.reasoning: Alternative hit-rate and quantitative analyses preserved the positive effect in all original participants. Lower modulation strength is explicitly accompanied by confirmation of the substantive observation.
